items.title: 63477_Joe Darensbourg oral history interview
items.q: I was having such a bad time, not really with Teddy but with a guy named Happy Cunwith(?) that owned the Four Hundred Club, I got so I didn't like him, and I wanted to get out of the band

ctx.x: What made you decide to go into the bandleading business? You'd been a sideman practically all your life...

I really didn't want to do it. But Helen, my wife, tried to talk me into it, and these people, like I said, made me an offer that was good. And I just wanted to... I was having such a bad time, not really with Teddy but with a guy named Happy Cunwith(?) that owned the Four Hundred Club, I got so I didn't like him, and I wanted to get out of the band -- me and Harvey Brooks both.
Because that was a good band you put together.
